text:
The Wild finally found out what a shootout feels like. Saturday in Vancouver was their first of the season, they went 0-for-3, Kirill Kaprizov hit the post, and a five-game winning streak ended. As NHL.com's Heather Rule noted, they are still 11-0-3 in their last 14. Minnesota has 39 points, 99% playoff chances by our numbers, and a 62% chance of winning the division.

Kaprizov carries his own 14-game point streak into San Jose (7 goals, 21 assists), and Matt Boldy has goals in three straight. Quinn Hughes, who matched Kaprizov's streak before leaving Thursday's win in Calgary after a collision, is out, with ESPN estimating a return on Wednesday. His absence falls hardest on Brock Faber, back from a skull fracture and up to 29:14 a night beside Jonas Brodin. Be honest about where the record comes from, though: a +35 goal difference on +18.8 expected, and Jesper Wallstedt's .923 save percentage, 18.2 goals better than expected, doing the lifting. Minnesota does control play, with 52% of the expected goals at five on five, but not by 35 goals' worth.

San Jose is 3-1-1 in its last five and has one of the league's most exciting young lines. Ivar Stenberg has moved beside Macklin Celebrini and Will Smith since Igor Chernyshov went on injured reserve, and his minutes are up to 20:05. Yaroslav Askarov has turned a rough last season (19.4 goals below expected) into 3.8 above this season. The Sharks still give up a lot, the second-most expected goals per 60 of anyone, and their penalty kill allows 0.96 expected goals a game against a Minnesota power play that creates 0.84. Kiefer Sherwood is also out.

The teams met on November 6, a 4-1 Minnesota win that the Wild deserved 75% of the time. Our numbers favor them again, 3.92 expected goals to 2.70. Dmitry Orlov is one assist from 300 for his career. Our sleeper is Minnesota's Bobby Brink, a third-liner with five high-danger shots in his last 10, at 17% to score.
headline: The Wild bring a 14-game point streak to San Jose
